finding.text: Once a queued voice mastermind starts, the bridge still thinks it is queued, and keeps thinking so until Servex restarts. `queued_why()` (RemoteMCP.js, diff line 127) reads `this.standins` before `agents.live`. The gate's stand-in (`Servex/Servex.js:1304`, `hold()`) always returns `state: "queued"` from `card()`, so the entry never clears. Every later ask on that connection says "waiting to start", and with a fallback set it is routed to the fallback forever. The fix is simpler too: drop `standins` and ask the gate itself, `this.servex.agents.queued_entry?.(id)` (`Servex/Servex.js:1185`). That also covers a queue restored after a restart, which the in-memory Map misses.

A `to` or fallback agent that is busy with other work has its words taken as the voice answer. `heard_event()` (diff lines 290–301) hands every delta of an agent to its oldest open ticket. When the turn ends without a reply file, `deliver()` makes those words the answer. So asking a working `vscode-mastermind`, or any running mastermind, can return the tail of an unrelated turn. The same race hits the voice mastermind if a new ask arrives while the last ask's turn is still running after its file was read. One fix: open the ticket's stream only after the `agent_msg` that carries this qid. Another: use turn-words as the answer only when the ticket's own message started that turn.

`Servex/ext/remote/readme.md:3` is stale. It still says `ask_mastermind` waits "up to a minute", and it does not name `voice_hear`, the `to` argument, `remote.fallback` / `REMOTE_MCP_FALLBACK` or `REMOTE_MCP_WAIT_MS`. A fresh agent reading only the readme would not know the bridge exists.

`Servex/ext/remote/doc/remote-tools.md:41` ("ask_mastermind never loses an answer") still opens with "waits up to a minute" and says `wait: false` returns `{ticket, note}`. It now waits 8 s and returns the whole ticket view. That section sits directly under the new bridge section, which contradicts it.

Requirement 3's "measure it" is only half met. The ack (2–3 ms) and first words (310 ms) were measured against the fake agent in `RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, and Opus's first sentence (8.6–8.7 s) by `first-words.mjs`. The live number waits on a Servex restart. `plan.md` says this, but nothing in the task folder is filed to run `measure.mjs --bridge` after the restart, so a fresh agent would need to be told.
`public/framework/ai/doc/voice-agents.md:45` still calls `wait:false` + `updates` "Yes, today's best". Once the bridge is live, that row should say the bridge replaced it.

The INSTRUCTIONS line and `cloud-voice-agent.md:69` say "later words ride along" on tool results. `ride()` carries only the say-first sentence and the final answer, not the words in between (only `voice_hear`'s `status`/`doing` shows progress). The wording promises a little more than the code does.

`.claude/skills/voice-mastermind/SKILL.md:14` still says "write the reply FIRST" (meaning the reply file). The new message says to stream one sentence before any tool call, and the file is optional when that sentence is the whole answer. The skill and the gateway prompt now give slightly different instructions; one sentence in the skill would line them up.

A `result` with `stopped: true` (agent stopped mid-turn) also ends a ticket with its partial words as the answer (`heard_event`, diff line 298). Skipping `event.stopped` there would match how `Sessions.heard()` treats it (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1442`).

The default fallback, `vscode-mastermind`, never streams, so it can lose an answer. The new message says "If your first sentence was the whole answer, skip the file" (`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js`, diff line 180). But a VS Code tab is an external agent: `Agents.send` hands it to `external.deliver()` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:613`), and no `delta`/`result` event ever reaches `heard_event`. A tab that follows the message and skips the file leaves its ticket at status "asked" forever, and nothing ever goes to the inbox. Fix: tell agents that are not in `agents.live` to always write the file, or say in the docs that say-first streaming works only for Servex SDK agents.

Test case 9 hides that gap. It fakes `vscode-mastermind` as a live streaming agent (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, diff line 418, then `live.set("vscode-mastermind", …)`), so "the fallback answers" passes for an agent shape the real fallback never has. Add one case with an external target that answers only through the reply file.

`.claude/skills/voice-mastermind/SKILL.md:14` still says "write the reply FIRST", meaning the reply file, before anything slow. The new "Say first" bullet just below says to stream one sentence before any tool call, and lets that sentence replace the file. Both point the same way, but line 14 should be reworded to match (the first review's note 8 is half done).

The loop in `heard_event` meant to answer "several queued asks" with one turn (diff line 302) only ever delivers `t`. Only the oldest ticket collects `words`, so `x.words` is empty for every other ticket. That is harmless, but the comment promises more than the code does.

Requirement 3's live numbers are still waiting on a Servex restart. `voice-agents.md` marks the bridge row "live after the next Servex restart" and quotes 3 ms / 8.7 s from the test door and `first-words.mjs`, which is honest. A later agent should re-run `measure.mjs --bridge` after the restart and replace the row.

A follow-up asked while the mastermind is still on the previous voice ask loses its answer. Ask B arrives while ask A's turn runs, so B is unarmed (`busy`, RemoteMCP.js diff line 183). B only arms when B is the oldest open ticket and a `result` arrives (`heard_event`, diff line 305). A's own result is handled for A, and the loop at diff line 312 skips the unarmed B. So B's own turn only arms it, its words are dropped, and if the mastermind followed "skip the file" (it was told it streams), B never gets an answer. The next unrelated turn's words then become B's answer. This is the bridge's main case: a slow ask returns "Not answered yet", the owner keeps talking and asks again. Fix: on any `result`, arm every open ticket that was unarmed when that turn started, not only `open[0]`. Add a test with two voice asks in a row to the same streaming agent, the second asked mid-turn.

An agent with more than one turn queued ahead of the ask arms after the first of them (`armed` is one turn deep). A minion's "done" message queued behind the running turn would then have its words taken as the answer. `Agent.queued` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:2203) could set how many results to skip.
`Servex/ext/remote/doc/remote-tools.md` (diff line 507) says "Tested in RemoteMCP.test.mjs (cases 6–10)". Case 11 (the tab that answers only by file) now exists too.

The voice mastermind's spawn prompt (`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:309`, "answer by writing plain text to it") still describes the file-only reply. Each message overrides it with SAY FIRST, but one clause there ("say one sentence first, as each message asks") would make the two agree.

Requirement 3's live numbers still wait on a Servex restart. This is filed as a task in `session.jsonl`, and the `voice-agents.md` row says "live after the next Servex restart", so a fresh agent can pick it up from the task folder.

`ahead()` counts the turns waiting in front of a new ask as `queue.items.length` (Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:419). But the SDK reads `queue.stream()` as soon as a message is pushed, so a message that arrives while the agent is working sits in the CLI, not in `items`. The CLI's own count is `queued_turn_count` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:2202). So when the voice mastermind is mid-turn and a minion's "done" message is already waiting, an ask gets `ahead = 1` when the true count is 2. When the minion's turn ends, `deliver()` falls back to that turn's words because the reply file isn't written yet (RemoteMCP.js:351), and the owner hears the minion report as the answer. The fix: count turns with `a.queue?.kinds?.length`, which gets one entry per pushed turn and drops one at each result (Agents.js:1781); check how compaction turns affect it. Then add a test whose fake agent keeps `items` empty while messages wait. Test case 12 can't catch this today, because its fake agent has no queue at all.

When an ask's turn count is wrong (finding 1, or a `priority: "now"` message that jumps the queue), the comment at RemoteMCP.js:417 says the answer still arrives by its reply file. But a streaming agent is told "If your first sentence was the whole answer, skip the file" (RemoteMCP.js:327), so there may be no file to fall back on. After fixing 1, reword that comment, or always ask for the file.

The bridge's speed hasn't been measured live yet. The 3 ms ack and the 0.3 s first words come from the test door with a fake agent. The 8.7 s first words come from first-words.mjs, not from a call through the bridge. voice-agents.md §4 says the bridge goes live after the next Servex restart; once it does, re-run `measure.mjs --bridge` and update that row.

This task folder has files that aren't committed: past-work.md, review.jsonl and review/ are untracked, and session.jsonl and inbox.jsonl have changes. plan.md, which holds the ask-first list, is committed, so a fresh agent can pick the task up from here. Commit the rest by path before the merge.

Servex/ext/remote/readme.md names `remote.fallback` but not where that file lives. It goes beside the token file (`RemoteMCP.fallback()`, RemoteMCP.js:266). Law 9 asks for the exact layout on disk, so add "beside the token file" to the readme line.

The brief asks to "check what hooks or `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` allow" for pushing into the VS Code tab, but nothing in the diff, plan.md or voice-agents.md mentions either one. voice-agents.md §4 covers only the inbox file + Monitor and the peer `SendMessage` (which never arrived). Add one row or line to §4 with what was found, or "not checked" plus a filed task.

`.claude/skills/voice-mastermind/SKILL.md:19` still says "Answer inside the tool's one-minute window … Reply within the minute". `ask_mastermind` now waits 8 s and the new "Say first" bullet replaces this, so cut that sentence or reword it to match.

`Servex/ext/remote/doc/cloud-voice-agent.md:88` and `:98` still describe the pre-bridge workflow ("`wait: false` returns a ticket at once", "Alternative workflow to try: never wait. Fire the ask (`wait: false`) …"). The new "Asking without waiting" section supersedes them. Mark them as history or point them at that section, so a voice agent doesn't follow the older advice.

The bridge's speed has still only been measured in the test door: ack 4 ms, first words 317 ms, answer 1.9 s (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs` passes in the worktree at 419d9fa81). The live measurement is filed as a task on the session record ("measure it live after the next Servex restart"), so this is tracked, not missing.

The test's fake agent shifts `queue.kinds` before it calls `watch` (RemoteMCP.test.mjs:422). The real `Agent.emit` calls `host.watch` first and shifts after (Agents.js:1771, 1781). `heard_event` never reads `kinds`, so nothing breaks today. But if a later change reads `ahead()` inside the listener, the test would hide an off-by-one. A one-line comment would cover it.
